{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.25) and historical prices show downward momentum.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes by applying a 10-15% dampening factor to the immediate next period.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast deviates > ±15% from 30-day moving average, adjust toward the average with a decay factor of 0.8 per period.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment shifts: if sentiment rises above 0.5, adjust forecast upward by 2-5% for the next 3 periods.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce volatility by applying a smoothing filter (e.g., exponential decay with α=0.3) to avoid overreaction to short-term noise.",
    "When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >20% underperformance), assume market correction and reduce next period’s forecast by 5-10%.",
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is below historical low, increase forecast by 3-7% to reflect bullish momentum."
  ]
}
